neighborhood_overview: Our beautiful Grove Park Historic District close to downtown is a safe, friendly neighborhood with well-lit sidewalks, wonderful gardens, parks, and a fantastic greenway linking to the center of Asheville.
host_about:
Welcome to Terrace Cottage!

For fifteen years we have enjoyed hosting visitors in our Asheville, North Carolina cottage from across the country and around the world including England and Ireland, Greece, Canada, Mexico and Cuba, Argentina, Japan and The Phillipines. We welcome guests from around the corner, across the US and our international visitors as well! Our college-age daughter grew up listening to many different languages in the driveway.

We enjoy traveling including work-and-play trips to Ireland, England, Sweden and Greece. Twenty years here at our residence built in 1926 and our adjacent Terrace Cottage was built in 2000.

We love working in our perennial beds and veggie gardens.

I'm an online entrepreneur designing and marketing wooden playthings for young people. I also collect and blog about vintage wooden toys.

My wife is a clinician with UNC-Chapel Hill School of Medicine. 

We love living in Asheville and are always happy to return home when away. It is a nationally-celebrated and uniquely beautiful mountain city overflowing with eclectic opportunities for enjoying first-rate dining, entertainment, crafts and artwork. The Blue Ridge Parkway entrance is ten minutes from our home, leading to the North Carolina Arboretum, Mount Pisgah, Craggy Gardens, and Mount Mitchell- the highest elevation east of the Rocky Mountains. 

I fly fish and welcome inquiries regarding our local waters. My favorite streams are under an hour away and have been rated in Trout Unlimited's Top 100. There are excellent fly shops and outfitters nearby if you need them.

Walking, running and cycling are huge in Asheville and there are too many options to mention from neighborhood greenways and hill climbs to maniacal day-longs as well, contact us for info. Our local runner's and cyclist's shops are just blocks away.

Speaking of walkable- ditto our supermarket and specialty/whole foods markets, cafes, coffee shops, local theater, pharmacies, UNC-Asheville, botanical gardens, awesome kid's parks and more.

Thanks for looking at Terrace Cottage and we welcome your inquiries!

neighborhood_overview:
Our charming basement apartment is situated in a serene and friendly neighborhood, offering a peaceful retreat while being conveniently close to some of Asheville's most delightful dining and entertainment options.

Dining and Culinary Delights:
You'll find an array of culinary delights just a short walk from your doorstep. Whether you're in the mood for artisanal pizza, fresh sushi, health-conscious fare, indulgent ice cream, or the best Italian cuisine in town, our neighborhood has it all:

Asheville Pizza and Brewing Company: A local favorite, known for its delectable pizzas and craft beers.

Zen Sushi: For the sushi enthusiasts, Zen Sushi offers a wide range of fresh and creative sushi rolls.

Green Sage: If you prefer health-conscious options, Green Sage serves up delicious and nourishing meals.

The Hop Ice Cream: Satisfy your sweet tooth with handcrafted ice cream flavors at The Hop.

Avenue M: Experience a delight
host_about:
I followed the whitewater to this beautiful mecca in the mountains.  I love all the amazing opportunities to be in the gorgeous natural beauty of this area.  So many rivers, waterfalls, trails, and views to enjoy.  Asheville also happens to be one of the coolest towns I've ever come across to hang out in.  Southern charm, for sure.  Lots of great live music, delicious restaurants, local festivals, amazing art scene, and a happening dance community.  Oh yeah, a healing arts mecca.  Plenty of yoga and therapeutic options around these parts.
I'll tell you where to find the best huevo rancheros you've ever had in your life!
I've lived in Asheville for 10 years now, and know the area pretty well from all of my exploration.  I have worked at the 5 star resort, The Grove Park Inn, and happen to live just one mile from this world famous Resort and Spa.  Being a massage therapist there, I can tell you which treatments will be perfect for you.  I have spent plenty of time at the Biltmore Estates and can suggest good walks to take there.

I am really easy-going and have been renting rooms in my house for many years to people who need a place to stay for weeks, months or sometimes years.  Guests will have a comfortable home away from home with easy flexibility within the house to come and go as you please. (must love music!)

We live in Asheville in the beautiful mountains of western North Carolina.

Allison works as a fourth grade teacher at Mills River Elementary School. Peter works as the Trails Coordinator at a regional land trust, Conserving Carolina. Both of us work to keep this region we love as wonderful as it is today, and make it even better for future generations.

We love to take road trips throughout the year. We have appreciated the kindness of many over the years who have let us stay in their home or camp in their yard, or have rented a room to us for a reasonable rate. For that reason, most hosts barely know that we are there. In appreciation for the kindness shown to us over the years, we pay it forward by being clean and courteous when we are guests in the homes of others, and we are seeking to host guests who are similarly self-sufficient and simply seeking a basic place for the night.

We look forward to you staying in our home!

name: Bed and breakfast in Asheville · 1 bedroom · 1 bed · 1 private bath
neighborhood_overview: Located in the Chestnut Hill Historical District of Asheville, we are a quick 10 minute walk to downtown and less than a mile from everything it has to offer.
host_about:
Emilie first fell in love with Asheville over 20 years ago when she attended Rockbrook Camp in the heart of a wooded mountain in Brevard, NC. Those mountains, so different from the beaches of her childhood, kept her coming back for ten years. There is something majestic about the Blue Ridge Mountains that blanket Western North Carolina, at over 1 billion years old, they are some of the oldest mountains in the entire world.

Arturo came to Asheville for the first time in 2012 and was quickly enamoured with the outdoor culture, so different from his 22 years in New York City, but so reminiscent of his childhood in the gentle hills of Puebla, Mexico. For him, it was a desire to start a family and a business and seek a better quality of life and he quickly found himself thirsty for everything that Asheville has to offer.

Emilie and Arturo met in 2008 while working together as sommeliers in the Lower East Side of Manhattan at The Ten Bells. Their working relationship was incredible, and over the next six years that relationship became a fine tuned machine- customers would always comment about the way they were able to seamlessly run the entire restaurant without even speaking. Learning the way one another worked over those first six years was the beginning of a true friendship that blossomed into love.

With 35 years of fine dining experience between the two, a Bed and Breakfast seemed like the perfect next adventure. Their penchant for hospitality and intuitive service and their true joy in meeting new people and making new friends put them in a unique position to choose their next path.

Emilie’s first Bed and Breakfast plan was written in the back of a college notebook when she was 18, wandering around Maine searching for the perfect wraparound porch. In 2011, she and Arturo decided to give those Bed and Breakfast dreams a trial run, and opened a small B&B in their East Village apartment. While tiny, it gave them a wonderful test-run on breakfast planning, scheduling, cleaning, decorating, recipe testing and conflict management. They loved it all!

The tri-lingual couple feel that they will bring a new, re-invented experience to the somewhat clichéd country B&B Inn. Asheville is no longer a sleepy town with boarded up buildings, it is a hub of restaurants, nightlife, music, beer and outdoor adventure. It’s not only the perfect place to call home, it is the perfect place to welcome someone into yours.

Llamasté is approximately 10 minutes to the Biltmore Estate and Village, 3 minutes to the Blue Ridge Parkway and 13 minutes to Downtown Asheville. It is an approximately 20 minute drive (in good traffic) and 14 miles from Asheville Regional Airport.

VERY CONVENIENTLY LOCATED!

host_about:
I am an artistic soul with a love of Nature, animals wild and domestic, good food, good wine and good conversation. I relish all kinds of music, especially World, Bluegrass and Celtic. Connecting deeply with Nature and animals, and with open-minded people is my delight.

A special note about the name Llamasté.....when I had the good fortune to become the Steward of this blessed mountain sanctuary, there were two llamas and two goats living here who clearly stated their preference to stay put, rather than go with their previous  beloved owners to much smaller and less green pastures. name: Cabin in Asheville · ★4.93 · 2 bedrooms · 2 beds · 1 bath
neighborhood_overview: The cabin sits just off New Leicester Highway. This property is unique in that, from the cabin looking out, you feel like you are out in the country. Long-range mountain views, beautiful sunsets, a barn, and cows in the pasture, give the feeling of being away from it all even though you are not. The cabin does sit on a hill, about 600 yards off the highway, so some road noise can be heard, however, you are just seconds away from everything. Just beyond the trees is the gas station, and just down the road less than a mile is the grocery store, Walgreens, and some fast food. Better yet, just 5 miles down the road is downtown Asheville and the interstate. Please note that we do relocate the cows in the winter from December thru March due to cold weather and freezing water.
host_about:
My name is Shauna. I have lived in the Asheville area since 2009. I met my husband here and we have been married since 2012. We have 2 children. A 5 year old girl and a 1 year old boy.  

After our first child was born I became a "work from home" mom, and now I oversee our rentals. We started our first rental in December of 2016 and I absolutely fell in love with doing it, so much so, that we started up another rental in March of 2018. I can't put my finger on what exactly I love about it, but I just do. I love the freedom it gives me to be with my kids and handle the "unexpected." I also love that it allows me to be more hands on with guests or handle issues or needs in person vs. over the phone or having someone else do it for me. 

5 things I can't live without.....
coffee
massages
doing anything and everything outdoors
giving my kids kisses and hugs everyday and playing with them
and, yeah....wine and beer

My husband and I are very laid back, fun, outdoorsy people. We love everything outdoors. You name it, we do it. We also love to travel, especial out of the country.
Favorite hobbies include gardening, canning, raising cows, fishing, mountain biking, hiking, and exploring new restaurants.

We are always on the go and it seems like something unexpected always happens or changes our plans, so I would have to say our life motto is, "just roll with the punches and deal with it as best you can." Nothing is perfect and stuff happens. How you handle it determines the end result.

neighborhood_overview: All of Asheville is at your fingertips from this home. Settled in a peaceful gem of a neighborhood, you will be just a walk away from historic Biltmore Village. host_about:
Sisters, Emily and Annie Hammer are California transplants with big hearts for Asheville. Passionate for travel and exploration, Asheville called us both to be part of the eclectic and vibrant tapestry of Western North Carolina. With seven years of “local” between us, we have immersed ourselves in our town and constantly explore this ever-changing canvas that is AVL.  With a longtime dream of working together as small business owners, we combined both our love of nesting (and all things home) and hospitality into a special combination. Thus, our business "Two Hammers" was born. Read more about us on our website (two-hammers) or find us on social media.

About Emily: Emily is a creative type, with a mind for business. When not playing host or designing properties and interiors, she can be found in her art studio dabbling and making art. From paper sculpting, collaging with vintage jewelry, teaching silk painting, block printing and needle felting, she loves to dabble. If not in her art studio, she’s probably dancing at her local dance studio of choice, where she spends way too much of her time. An avid foodie and culture seeker, she is always searching for hidden gems in town and surrounding area. A self-proclaimed history and architecture “nerd”, she is the first person to talk about the Biltmore and other local historical spots. She lives outside of Biltmore Village with her beloved dog, Kaia, and cat, Jezebel.

About Annie: Annie is a natural born helper. She has always had a passion and heart for serving others. That passion has led her down many different paths, whether that's studying social work at Warren Wilson College, doing various volunteer work or, most recently, earning her 200 hour yoga teacher training.  Being in the hospitality industry felt like a natural fit and an extension of her talents. With her added entrepreneurial spirit, mind for business and flare for, running Two Hammers with her sister Emily, is a dream come true. In her free time, you can find Annie taking dance classes, practicing yoga, spoiling her pup Josie and exploring the food scene in Asheville.

I now love sharing this space and hearing  feedback I get about the design, the light and feel of the space.

  I do hope you enjoy Asheville as much as I do !

I moved to Sausalito, California where I became a Strategy Implementation Consultant. As a bilingual and bicultural person, I was able to work  in 11 countries in Western Europe, South America, and North America. It was a great life, and I met wonderful people from all over the world.    I am also a song-writer and an author, and love music of all kinds from all parts of the world.

     In 2001, my husband and I moved to Asheville, NC, and we love it! Being in the mountains, in a glorious little town is perfect for us in our retirement phase of life, or our "repurposed" phase, as my husband likes to say.   
     We have two small dogs (a chihuahua mix and a mountain feist, both under 16 pounds). 
     We live on two acres, surrounded by wonderful, local neighbors that we are blessed to have around us.

     We're easy going, like hosting friends, family and our AirBnB guests. Kelle was in the hotel and restaurant business decades ago, and this is a gentle step back into something she found much fun to pursue. 

Life is good, and we would  love to share it with you.

name: Vacation home in Asheville · ★5.0 · 7 bedrooms · 12 beds · 4.5 baths
neighborhood_overview: The house is perched above the French Broad River, across from the Biltmore Estate. It's near a park with bike paths leading into Downtown Asheville and New Belgium Brewery. Launch a tube from the new boat ramp directly across from the house.
host_about:
Our houses are much nicer than they appear on this site.   Airbnb does not allow us to use our own photographs on two of our listings so you may need to go on our internal website.   It is easy to find us with a simple search for "Upstream way"   That is the name of our street.

We also have lots of cool video and virtual tours.   Lesley, my right hand, has compiled volumes of information on Asheville and travel tips for your visit.

Anyone who uses Airbnb knows you have to invest a lot of time and energy to find the good rentals in Asheville, NC.   The city made it illegal after we got our permits and there are way too many folks trying to book far too few homes.    

We built our new website so you will not get tricked with photoshop.    Our 5 houses on Upstream Way are the real thing.   

My development company built the whole street so we are not like a normal house you find in a random location next door to owner occupied homes in a residential neighborhood.   

I have stayed in those before and you are not exactly welcomed by the other homeowners.   The neighbors tend to dislike the constant coming and going of tourists in a family neighborhood.

I once lived next to an illegal Airbnb property and came up with a solution.

We are literally an entire resort of vacation rentals all side by side.   Your neighbor is also here for a special occasion and will probably offer you a beverage.

You can bring anywhere from 1 to 100 people and have the whole place to yourself.

It is without equal.   The best you can do is copy us, but nobody can get the permits.

Bachelorette’s and Wedding Parties got us started but we shy away from them now.   

We will host a lot of different occasions and you need not worry if you want to have a bachelor party or bachelorette.   

I make it no secret that we want to focus on corporate executives who visit for team building and holistic health retreats, but we don't judge your motive.

We welcome everyone the same way.

You can depend on us because we deliver what you are expecting and then we go as far beyond as is humanly possible.

My team has some of the best and brightest.   My right hand is Lesley, my left hand is Aracely, her children Kasey and Brian are her right and left hands.  If something needs repair, Leo & Kaden are available.

I have known each person on my staff from years and years of time together.   I am not easy to work for.   Trust me.   

At times, I have no idea why these people are such hard workers and trusted friends. 
With Covid-19 we all work for a fraction of our former compensation.

Somehow; you and I both got lucky.    We survived this and I see the light at the end of the tunnel.

Ok, I will wrap this up:

If you reach out you will never get an answering service or a stranger.   

We are not property managers.    We are the folks who built this place.

We built it for you.

You don't arrive here by accident.

So far, 217 Airbnb customers have reviewed us.   Keep in mind, that represents thousands of people as our average group is 12 people.

Nobody has ever given us below 5 stars.   Not even once.   Not even close.

Plus, you are welcome to check a lot of other websites and our own internal software.  

Thousands of people have come here and they seem to be happy with us and we often see them again and again.

We cost more for a reason:   

You get more.

You come for a special occasion.   

You leave with a priceless memory.

Then we plan for the next one.

I think that is why we are almost booked out into '22.

All the best,
jay

name: Cabin in Asheville · ★4.81 · 1 bedroom · 2 beds · 1 bath
neighborhood_overview:
This home is located on the top of Spivey Mountain; at 3,300 ft. elevation, it's the mountain in closest proximity to West Asheville. It's a quiet neighborhood- in fact, you can't see any neighbors from our property, unless you count the wildlife! You can find turkeys, woodpeckers, rabbits and even bears on the mountain!

Bustling West Asheville is just an 8-10 minute drive down the mountain, where you can find dozens of great restaurants, bars, local shops, services and anything else you could need! You can get into Downtown Asheville in less than 15 minutes from this home. Ubers are usually $10-$20 to downtown, depending on the time of week.
host_about:
Originally from New York, I have been living in Asheville, NC since 2007 and am "almost" a Southerner. I am a small business owner with 3 pet supply stores. My husband and I work hard so we can play hard- we love to travel and Airbnb is such a unique way to really get to know new places and have a more authentic experience!

 After moving further out into the country, we decided to share our home in West Asheville with visitors, and share what we love most about this beautiful area!

neighborhood_overview:
Biltmore Village is the best location to be on a visit to Asheville! The Biltmore Estate is a must-see on a visit to Asheville. Besides being the largest, privately owned house in the U.S. and built by the Vanderbilt family, there are so many things to do and see on the property besides touring the amazing home. The colorful gardens, Conservatory, serene Bass Pond Waterfall, walking paths along the French Broad River, winery and kids petting zoo are just some of the things that you can plan. Seeing the 7,000 acre grounds can take days to cover. The convenience of our home being a 1/2 mile from the Biltmore Estate entrance makes for a seamless visit.

Biltmore Village has many wonderful restaurants and shops you can WALK to. One of our favorite spots is Well Bred Bakery - consistently receives #1 bakery in Asheville each year...and guests can walk five minutes to it! Opposite side of the street is Corner Kitchen with fresh farm to table meals. At the bottom of our hill is Fig
host_about:
“Travel changes you. As you move through this life and this world you change things slightly, you leave marks behind, however small. And in return, life—and travel—leaves marks on you.”  – Anthony Bourdain.

We LIVE to travel! Heather spent many years working in the airline industry which allowed us to see 40+ countries. The Anthony Bourdain show “No Reservations”  sums up our travel style. We tend to book the first night to recover from jet lag and then keep the rest of the trip open. We like to see where our travels want to take us. Seeking out the “undiscovered” places and truly connecting with locals is what we are all about. Some of our favorites: Luang Prabang / Bagan / Zanzibar / Bali / Colombia / Ronda (got engaged) / Samana, Dominican Republic (got married) / Chicago / Isla Holbox (shhhh, keep it a secret). Through many of these travels Airbnb has been a big piece of the puzzle.  

The two of us met in Aspen, CO. Heather is originally from Chicago and Mark from Virginia Beach. Although Heather loved city life her wanderlust brought her to Aspen for thirteen years.  Mark had been living in Washington D.C. doing the daily grind as an architect and had heard about a firm in Aspen that was hiring. He jumped on the chance and never looked back!  Aspen was a fantastic place to live and truly enjoy life. It taught us that you can live more simply and have a healthier quality of life. 

After a long stint out west and with a child on the way we decided it was time to be closer to family. We had a list of 30 towns all over the midwest and eastern U.S. which we either visited or did research on. After visiting Asheville we knew it was our next stop in life. Mark has opened his own office and Heather teaches at a creative arts center while studying interior design. Besides continuing to travel, we hike with our son and two dogs as often as possible and love checking out the awesome breweries and restaurants Asheville has to offer. We've also just begun hosting on Airbnb and really enjoy meeting fellow travelers and hosting them in our guest suite. 

We hope to inspire others to get out of their comfort zone and check out other places and people on this amazing planet! 

"Not until we are lost do we begin to understand ourselves." 
- Henry David Thoreau

name: Home in Asheville · ★4.90 · 1 bedroom · 1 bed · 1 private bath
neighborhood_overview: Quiet shady neighborhood, with lots of kids and diversity. Our neighborhood is a mixture of ranch style homes, Victorian homes and cute bungalows. Great for running, walking and biking. An abundance of trees and flowers.
host_about:
Born in NC, attended UNC-Chapel Hill and got a degree in Journalism. My mom's side of the family has lived in Western North Carolina for the past century and a half. I have relatives buried in the Riverside Cemetery, which we can see from our backyard.
However, I lived most of my adult life on the West Coast. After college, I drove west in a school bus and eventually landed outside Eugene, OR, next to a creek, grew lots of my food, and had a sewing business, selling at the Saturday Market, Circle of Hands and craft fairs up and down the West Coast.
I have been to all 50 states, Canada, several Central American countries, Caribbean islands and Europe. I LOVE meeting people from all around the world and have studied conflict resolution in large groups of people using World Work. I am a therapist full time, offering massage therapy as well as Bodywisdom Therapy, helping people unravel the messages of their bodies, at a location on Merrimon Avenue. I speak a bit of French and Spanish, but am alas, no longer fluent.
My son and I moved back to WNC several years ago to be near my Mom, who lives in Yancey County. I know some sweet areas to visit around the area and are including them in a notebook in the rooms. 
I love being able to offer people a centrally located place to enjoy what WNC has to offer, as well as a prime walking neighborhood to have access to downtown Asheville hotspots. 
I turned both bedrooms and bathrooms downstairs into places that I would like to visit myself, using art from my own collection, and textures and colors that I love.
We have friends and family over on a regular basis so there is a bit of hustle and bustle at times. If you have children, or like to come and go and appreciate the outdoors, you will fit right in! If you want privacy, the private entrance and keypad will fit your needs. If you want total peace and quiet, I am afraid we won't be your cup of tea.
Living lightly on the earth is a core value for me so we recycle as much as possible, and keep our throwaway consumables to a minimum. 
Life is for loving, sharing and making the world better wherever we can.

I speak a bit of French and Spanish, but am alas, no longer fluent.
My son and I moved back to WNC several years ago to be near my Mom, who lives in Yancey County. I know some sweet areas to visit around the area and are including them in a notebook in the rooms. 
I love being able to offer people a centrally located place to enjoy what WNC has to offer, as well as a prime walking neighborhood to have access to downtown Asheville hotspots. 
I turned both bedrooms and bathrooms downstairs into places that I would like to visit myself, using art from my own collection, and textures and colors that I love.

Life is for loving, sharing and making the world better wherever we can.

neighborhood_overview: Because the street is nestled alongside a river, the way out is all uphill. (Cyclists need to know these things!) host_about:
Hey - I'm Christine.

I moved to Asheville in the early 90's to escape Northern Virginia and my post-college cubicle job. I wanted to be a songwriter...which, as you can guess, thrilled my parents to no end.  

Turns out, Asheville was the perfect place to be creative, get quiet, wake the heck up - and spend the next 15 years as a touring performing songwriter on my own record label. (Shared stages with everyone from The Beach Boys to John Mayer to Nanci Griffith - and made 7 CD's along the way.)

In 2010, as a result of requests from so many creative entrepreneurial types (and being burnt out from 250 days a year on the road), I started a business coaching company here in Asheville. That became an online training resource, and we've hosted clients from all over the world at our retreats and events here. These days, I spend more time on Zoom than anything else. :)

Hosting guests has been an unexpected joy and new passion for me.  I love being able to provide all the amenities and experiences for travelers and vacationers and work-from-homers... mostly based on 15 years of staying in every hotel (ahem, and motel) chain and city across the U.S.  I'm still learning so much.

I love all things nature. Trees, birds, bears, mountains, dirt. I strive to contribute the creative and natural spirit of this precious area, even as it grows at a crazy pace.

name: Guest suite in Asheville · ★5.0 · 2 bedrooms · 2 beds · 1 bath
neighborhood_overview:
West Asheville is THE place to be these days in Asheville. It offers a subset of everything Downtown--amazing restaurants, live music, shopping, cafes, farmer's markets, craft creations from ice cream to beer to cider to croissants-with it's own artsy, funky vibe including murals, recycle shops, and artisan-made gifts and goods. From the Kimono Cottage you are just a few hundred meters' walk from Haywood Rood, the artery of the West Asheville arts and business district.

We are located in a safe and quiet neighborhood that is great for strolls and jogs. There are several parks within 1/2 mile and several greenway trails about 1 mile from the house. There are also several grocery stores in easy 5 min walking distance, as well as a post office, drug store, hardware store and urgent care. Without even getting in your car, our neighborhood gives you convenient access to everything you need and a unique taste of what makes Asheville well, Asheville!
host_about:
Hi! We are Gen, Anya, Sachi and Satsuki! Satsuki, also called May, is originally from Amami Oshima, Japan and lived in California for many years before transplanting to North Carolina to live with her son Gen and daughter-in-law Anya and their daughter Sachi. We opened the Kimono Cottage as a family project and love hosting visitors and sharing Japanese culture.

May Peace Prevail On Earth.

I enjoy giving tips on the things I enjoy in my area - mountain trails, music venues, microbreweries, eclectic restaurants, dancing, festivals, urban walking/biking/running, water activities.  The same things I'll enjoy doing/exploring in your area.

Located in East Asheville in the 28805 zip code, Haw Creek was named for the native Black Haw shrub or small tree (Viburnum prunifolium) that grew more abundantly years ago along the moist soils of the valley, especially along Haw Creek itself.

Haw Creek valley’s southern boundary extends from US Highway 70/Tunnel Road at I-240 eastward along Tunnel Road to Maple Springs Road. Its west boundary is formed by Piney Mountain/Bear Mountain ridge; Town Mountain creates the northern boundary; and the Blue Ridge Parkway stretches along most of its eastern border.

Haw Creek was settled in the early 1800’s as a farming community with the first school established in 1842 on the site of the present day Bethesda Cemetery. Haw Creek has two main entrances with very narrow roads throughout the valley. Arden is also home to several great parks and outdoor recreational areas. The North Carolina Arboretum, for example, is a must-visit destination for nature lovers, featuring extensive gardens, hiking trails, and a variety of educational exhibits and programs.

neighborhood_overview:
Our neighborhood is the charming Chestnut Hill Historical District of downtown Asheville. We are an easy 10 minute walk to the main area of downtown, a 12 minute drive to the Biltmore Estate, a 15 minute drive north for the Blue Ridge Parkway and Folk Art Center, a 15 minute drive to the NC Arboretum (Discount Shoes is on the way) and the BRP headed South to Mt Pisgah, a 10 minute drive to the River Arts District, a 5 minute drive to the breweries of the South Slope and 22 minute drive to the Asheville Regional Airport.
Our neighborhood itself has a couple of wonderful lunch cafés, three restaurants open for dinner only, the best butcher shop in town that has grab-and-go sandwiches, prepared meals and outrageous sausages and meats and of course we are only two blocks to Trader Joe's, Harris Teeter supermarkets and three blocks to Whole Foods.
host_about:
Emilie first fell in love with Asheville over 20 years ago when she attended Rockbrook Camp in the heart of a wooded mountain in Brevard, NC. Those mountains, so different from the beaches of her childhood, kept her coming back for ten years. There is something majestic about the Blue Ridge Mountains that blanket Western North Carolina, at over 1 billion years old, they are some of the oldest mountains in the entire world.

Arturo came to Asheville for the first time in 2012 and was quickly enamoured with the outdoor culture, so different from his 22 years in New York City, but so reminiscent of his childhood in the gentle hills of Puebla, Mexico. For him, it was a desire to start a family and a business and seek a better quality of life and he quickly found himself thirsty for everything that Asheville has to offer.

Emilie and Arturo met in 2008 while working together as sommeliers in the Lower East Side of Manhattan at The Ten Bells. Their working relationship was incredible, and over the next six years that relationship became a fine tuned machine- customers would always comment about the way they were able to seamlessly run the entire restaurant without even speaking. Learning the way one another worked over those first six years was the beginning of a true friendship that blossomed into love.

With 35 years of fine dining experience between the two, a Bed and Breakfast seemed like the perfect next adventure. Their penchant for hospitality and intuitive service and their true joy in meeting new people and making new friends put them in a unique position to choose their next path.

Emilie’s first Bed and Breakfast plan was written in the back of a college notebook when she was 18, wandering around Maine searching for the perfect wraparound porch. In 2011, she and Arturo decided to give those Bed and Breakfast dreams a trial run, and opened a small B&B in their East Village apartment. While tiny, it gave them a wonderful test-run on breakfast planning, scheduling, cleaning, decorating, recipe testing and conflict management. They loved it all!

The tri-lingual couple feel that they will bring a new, re-invented experience to the somewhat clichéd country B&B Inn. Asheville is no longer a sleepy town with boarded up buildings, it is a hub of restaurants, nightlife, music, beer and outdoor adventure. It’s not only the perfect place to call home, it is the perfect place to welcome someone into yours.

neighborhood_overview:
Just across the French Broad River from downtown, West Asheville (28806) is a mecca for originality. For the past few years, people have flocked to this funky neighborhood, either to visit or buy a quaint cottage within walking distance of the many new businesses that have opened in the area.

Haywood Road has been the main street of West Asheville for more than a century. Old buildings are now home to modern businesses, but the street still has a small hometown feel. As you walk down the street, you will see old buildings renovated for new businesses side-by-side with second- and third-generation shops. There are now many restaurants, breweries, pubs with frequent live music, bakeries, a variety of resale consignment shops, vintage clothing boutiques and even a half-dozen record shops lining the road that appeal to visitors interested in sampling the unique, bohemian flavor of Asheville.

Being an enthusiastic traveler, I also know the invaluable feeling I get when I rest my head at the end of the day on a comfortable pillow after a long train/plane/car ride. neighborhood_overview: The small town of Woodfin, NC rests along the banks of the French Broad River and its convenient location next to I-26 makes for a quick 5-minute drive to downtown Asheville. Filled with grit and charm, this historic suburban neighborhood is currently undergoing a fast-paced revival with the expansion of the River Arts District (RAD) and French Broad River Greenway Project. Breweries, restaurants, and coffee shops are overflowing from the nearby RAD. Our neighbors are lively and friendly, and you’re likely to get a small-town wave. These are good people. Please respect our neighbors by driving slow.
host_about:
I grew up on the Texas border near South Padre Island. I moved to Asheville in (Phone number hidden by Airbnb) from Austin, TX soon after graduating with a degree in mechanical engineering. The mountains called my name, and my would-be manager also called my name (to offer me a job),  so I set out on the 17hr drive and only looked back once...because I thought I saw a bear.

 I began my career servicing CTs, MRIs, and X-ray systems throughout Western North Carolina. If I'm not working on the house or hanging with the fam, my free time is spent playing outdoors - kayak fishing, mountain biking, and rock climbing. 

If there's an opportunity to go fishing, I usually take the bait. I own a small fleet of fishing kayaks and like to take day trips out on the local waters to pursue bass, trout and gorgeous scenery. If you're in the neighborhood to catch some fish, let me know and Ill try to give you some tips on where to go. 

Asheville is a mountain biker's paradise. There's an expansive network of trail systems all throughout the surrounding forests lands and hitting the trails with the gang is a surefire way to put a smile on my face. IMO its the best way to submerse yourself in these mountains and take in all their beauty. If you're itching for a thrilling downhill adventure or a casual bike ride through the mountains, reach out and I can point you in the right direction. 

My relationship with rock climbing is fickle; I'm either climbing or I'm not. I love it because by nature it puts you by nature. But if the fish are biting, its hard to pull me from a kayak to climb a 300 ft bluff. 

I also love music, food, and beer. If Asheville's beer and culinary scene is what brought you here, I am happy to offer advice. Let me know!

name: Chalet in Asheville · ★5.0 · 1 bedroom · 1 bed · 1 bath
neighborhood_overview:
Located in Kenilworth on Beaucatcher Mountain.

You will be close to all the fun outings, restaurants and shops, so it will definitely be easier for you to experience Asheville’s unique culture, art, cuisine, nature and much more!  You really are staying in one of the best locations in the city of Asheville.   

A little historical fact about Kenilworth area for your reference:
Per the kenilworthresidentsassociation.org site, Kenilworth, touted as Asheville’s 'Pioneer Suburb,' was founded in 1914. It is located between downtown Asheville and Biltmore Village and the Biltmore Estate. Situated on high land above the Swannanoa River, Kenilworth is one of Asheville’s oldest neighborhoods and was once its own town before getting annexed by the City of Asheville in 1929.
host_about:
Our family visited Asheville, NC, during one of our sightseeing tours across the United States, and we instantly fell in love with the city - so much so that we decided to purchase a vacation house there!  And the minute we stepped inside the Zurich Swiss Chalet property, we knew it was the one. 

Our adorable chalets combine our love for serene, picturesque getaways with our desire to remain close to the city's restaurants and shops. Because of how lovely it is and its unique location within the City of Asheville, we decided to share it with others.  

Hopefully, you'll enjoy it as much as we do!

name: Home in Asheville · 2 bedrooms · 2 beds · 2 baths
neighborhood_overview:
The ‘Lil Wedgie’ got its nick-name due to our proximity to the Wedge Brewery, my favorite! I invite you to come and enjoy the bustling West Asheville scene. It is a three minute walk from New Belgium Brewery, the River Arts District (RAD), and the Asheville Greenway. The heart of West Asheville is a 10-minute walk. There, you’ll find great restaurants, bars, breweries, music venues and coffee shops. To the east from the Li’l Wedgie, it’s less than 15 minutes by foot (or a quick Uber ride) to downtown Asheville and the famed South Slope! Enjoy our wonderful mountain town’s eclectic arts scene, dozens of world-class restaurants, breweries, and distilleries. If you’re a foodie, welcome to Paradise!

By the way, we are also home to great outdoor activities such as hiking, biking, water sports, and rock climbing. The Bent Creek Experimental Forest hiking and biking trail system is a 15-minute drive and Pisgah/DuPont/Brevard 30-minutes to an hour away by car.

Just across the French Broad River from downtown, West Asheville (28806) is a mecca for originality. For the past few years, people have flocked to this funky neighborhood, either to visit or buy a quaint cottage within walking distance of the many new businesses that have opened in the area.

name: Guesthouse in Asheville · 1 bedroom · 1 bed · 1 bath
neighborhood_overview:
Our neighborhood is the charming Chestnut Hill Historical District of downtown Asheville. We are an easy 10 minute walk to the main area of downtown, a 12 minute drive to the Biltmore Estate, a 15 minute drive north for the Blue Ridge Parkway and Folk Art Center, a 15 minute drive to the NC Arboretum (Discount Shoes is on the way) and the BRP headed South to Mt Pisgah, a 10 minute drive to the River Arts District, a 5 minute drive to the breweries of the South Slope and 22 minute drive to the Asheville Regional Airport.
Our neighborhood itself has a couple of wonderful lunch cafés, three restaurants open for dinner only, the best butcher shop in town that has grab-and-go sandwiches, prepared meals and outrageous sausages and meats and of course we are only two blocks to Trader Joe's, Harris Teeter supermarkets and three blocks to Whole Foods.
host_about:
Emilie first fell in love with Asheville over 20 years ago when she attended Rockbrook Camp in the heart of a wooded mountain in Brevard, NC. Those mountains, so different from the beaches of her childhood, kept her coming back for ten years. There is something majestic about the Blue Ridge Mountains that blanket Western North Carolina, at over 1 billion years old, they are some of the oldest mountains in the entire world.

Arturo came to Asheville for the first time in 2012 and was quickly enamoured with the outdoor culture, so different from his 22 years in New York City, but so reminiscent of his childhood in the gentle hills of Puebla, Mexico. For him, it was a desire to start a family and a business and seek a better quality of life and he quickly found himself thirsty for everything that Asheville has to offer.

Emilie and Arturo met in 2008 while working together as sommeliers in the Lower East Side of Manhattan at The Ten Bells. Their working relationship was incredible, and over the next six years that relationship became a fine tuned machine- customers would always comment about the way they were able to seamlessly run the entire restaurant without even speaking. Learning the way one another worked over those first six years was the beginning of a true friendship that blossomed into love.

With 35 years of fine dining experience between the two, a Bed and Breakfast seemed like the perfect next adventure. Their penchant for hospitality and intuitive service and their true joy in meeting new people and making new friends put them in a unique position to choose their next path.

Emilie’s first Bed and Breakfast plan was written in the back of a college notebook when she was 18, wandering around Maine searching for the perfect wraparound porch. In 2011, she and Arturo decided to give those Bed and Breakfast dreams a trial run, and opened a small B&B in their East Village apartment. While tiny, it gave them a wonderful test-run on breakfast planning, scheduling, cleaning, decorating, recipe testing and conflict management. They loved it all!

The tri-lingual couple feel that they will bring a new, re-invented experience to the somewhat clichéd country B&B Inn. Asheville is no longer a sleepy town with boarded up buildings, it is a hub of restaurants, nightlife, music, beer and outdoor adventure. It’s not only the perfect place to call home, it is the perfect place to welcome someone into yours.

neighborhood_overview: Few neighborhoods express the rich architectural heritage and vitality of Asheville better than the Montford Historic District.  The affluent Montford Area Historic District features distinctive Queen Anne, Arts and Crafts, and Colonial Revival houses, many restored as B&Bs. Henry are among those buried in the sprawling Riverside Cemetery, which has gardens and statue-topped mausoleums (walking distance).  Montford is a very walkable neighborhood close to downtown and offers multiple parks including Montford Park for tennis and pickle ball, or an outdoor yoga class.  Park is 1/4 mile away.

name: Home in Asheville · 2 bedrooms · 2 beds · 1 bath
neighborhood_overview:
Just across the French Broad River from downtown, West Asheville (28806) is a mecca for originality. For the past few years, people have flocked to this funky neighborhood, either to visit or buy a quaint cottage within walking distance of the many new businesses that have opened in the area.

Haywood Road has been the main street of West Asheville for more than a century. Old buildings are now home to modern businesses, but the street still has a small hometown feel. As you walk down the street, you will see old buildings renovated for new businesses side-by-side with second- and third-generation shops. There are now many restaurants, breweries, pubs with frequent live music, bakeries, a variety of resale consignment shops, vintage clothing boutiques and even a half-dozen record shops lining the road that appeal to visitors interested in sampling the unique, bohemian flavor of Asheville.

name: Home in Asheville · 1 bedroom · 1 bed · 1 shared bath
neighborhood_overview: The house is on a quiet residential street with very little passing car or foot traffic. The neighborhood is located near a housing project and the Asheville Survival Project, which supports local homeless folk. These might make the area feel a bit rough as you drive through, but our spot is tucked away and safe-feeling, and I've never had a problem with crime or any other disturbances in the 2 years I've been here. I also have security cameras covering the front of the property. The children at the preschool down the street love afternoon walks in the neighborhood and the green space across the street is the site of many community picnics and birthday parties. We're close to all the fun stuff on Haywood Road (shops, cafe, restaurants, bars, markets), and also to the lovely Carrier Park along the French Broad river. We're a little over a mile away from the River Arts District.

neighborhood_overview:
Malvern Hills is one of the oldest and friendliest neighborhoods in West Asheville. It once hosted a wellness center complete with soaking pools fed by a natural spring that now feeds Canie Creek. You can still see the remains of the retreat that burned down in 1891 at the bottom of our road near the greenway entrance.

We are one of the few areas in West Asheville to enjoy sidewalks lining all roads. Those walkways in addition to a greenway and creek mean you'll encounter lots of locals on their daily walk. The neighborhood hosts multiple block parties throughout the year - Halloween, 4th of July, multiple ice cream socials, greenway clean-up days, etc...

To learn more about our neighborhood and upcoming events, visit malvernhills dot org. The archive section has great info on the history of both our neighborhood and West Asheville.

Come and experience for yourself why residents love calling Asheville home.

name: Home in Asheville · 1 bedroom · 1 bed · 1 bath
neighborhood_overview: Just west of the desirable historic West Asheville neighborhood lies our quiet community. The architecture is a pleasant mix of larger, stately 1920s homes, small bungalows, brick tudor cottages, and mid-century ranch houses. The lots are of a generous size and are well-maintained. It's a neighborhood enveloped in natural beauty and mountain vistas, with amazing proximity to a wide range of amenities. Boasting broad sky views and the interconnected neighborhood makes for easy evening strolls and impromptu front yard gatherings. Patton Avenue provides quick access to downtown Asheville and I-40, while the western end of the neighborhood is bordered by Canie Creek. This small creek winds through large wooded tracts of land that create a wildlife haven; frequently spotted are deer, fox, migratory neotropical birds, and wild turkey.

name: Home in Asheville · ★5.0 · 1 bedroom · 2 beds · 1 bath
neighborhood_overview:
West Asheville: where anything goes and everyone is welcome! Just beyond downtown and across from the French Broad River sits West Asheville - a neighborhood with a vibe all of its own. Anchored by the walkable two-and-a-half-mile-long Haywood Road corridor, this trendy neighborhood has enough eateries, coffee spots, stores and things to do that warrant repeat exploration. From locally-sourced restaurants and quirky shops to bustling breweries and lively music venues, West Asheville is full of unique treasures and creative characters to discover. Check it out and see why locals love to call West Asheville home. (thanks to exploreasheville for the description!)

And a few more local recs, can't help myself:

Go for a stroll, run, or bike on the French Broad Greenway. 8+ miles of paved Greenway just a few blocks away (I run there most days). Lovely river views, folks walking and rolling by, and fresh air.

Grab a coffee at Home Ground or Summit. Or a beer
host_about: Hi there! I'm an Asheville native who is excited to share my growing mountain town with others. After living in CA for 20 years, I joyfully returned with my family. I love the French Broad Greenway and its possibilities for being outside. My husband, two kids, and I play there daily -- running, walking, biking, scooting, skating, hammocking, reading, tubing, or kayaking, often with our little pup. Hope to see you soon!
